decisions.title: Bind every anchor record to a document identity that lives in the CRDT state
decisions.body: An anchor record carries the identity of the document it was captured in, and resolution refuses any record whose identity does not match the document it is offered to. The identity is minted once when a document is created and travels inside the CRDT state, so it survives editing, saving, reloading and replica merges, while a re-import or a fork receives a new one. A content hash was rejected on both counts: it changes whenever the document is edited, and two documents holding the same text are still two documents. Link endpoints in the annotation plane therefore name a pair, document and record, because a record id is only unique inside one document.

decisions.title: Recover an unresolved anchor when its quote plus one affix matches uniquely
decisions.body: Phase 1 policy for re-attaching a standoff anchor whose CRDT position no longer resolves: search the document for the stored quote, and accept a hit when the exact text is unique and at least one affix (prefix or suffix) overlaps the stored context by a few characters. Rationale at the time: string context is cheap evidence of identity and keeps recovery rates high. Superseded because an affix overlap is not evidence of identity - short shared fragments cross a small threshold by accident, so the rule re-attached anchors to other sentences under ordinary edits (whole-block deletion, in-place replacement).

decisions.title: Recover an anchor only on CRDT evidence, never on string similarity alone
decisions.body: Recovery is attempted only when the CRDT says the anchored block itself disappeared, and it is accepted only when the stored block item id is still live in the document. Character survival inside a resolved range is judged by the identity of the captured characters, not by string similarity. Deleted-character evidence and in-place replacement both block recovery outright. When in doubt the anchor stays orphaned; the cost in recovery rate is measured rather than assumed.

decisions.title: Accept capture evidence only when it agrees with the record's other selectors
decisions.body: Provenance is accepted only when the captured character identities cover exactly as many characters as the stored quote, and a migration may only downgrade a record, never fill in evidence it does not have. Trusting the version number written in the file was the defect: a migration that fills the capture field from the current document state revives the very mis-resolution the guard exists to stop. Character identities cannot be copied out of the current state without contradicting the stored quote, so this check has teeth that a version number does not. Records that fail it take the explicit-orphan path.

decisions.title: Keep the link plane in one store outside ontology/ with a dedicated integrity checker
decisions.body: Cross-plane links live in a single JSON store under tools/plane-editor/, not in the knowledge graph. The graph tools only scan ontology/, so a store placed outside it cannot re-enter the graph by accident, which satisfies the no-reintroduction rule mechanically. The price is that SHACL and reachability no longer guard these edges, so a dedicated checker (check_links.py) carries endpoint existence, type vocabulary and boundary rules instead. Rejected alternatives: widening anchorTarget in the schema, and an editor-local store that opens no graph contact point at all.

decisions.title: Start the link and decision planes in parallel, defer anchor binding to the C1 gate
decisions.body: The link store and the decision plane are authored immediately; only binding a text anchor as a link endpoint waits for the anchor-misresolution gate. Links therefore target record identifiers, never text positions, until that gate passes. The measured baseline that made parallel work acceptable is the stale lane at 93.3 percent selector durability with zero misresolution in the measured scenarios.
